text: Lessons 9 through 11 all come together here, in one complete script that actually provisions a real Azure storage account, start to finish — the same official SDK, the same client pattern, and the same credential chain, doing real work instead of just being explained.

The script opens exactly the way Lessons 10 and 11 predicted: one import per service family — ResourceManagementClient from azure-mgmt-resource, StorageManagementClient from azure-mgmt-storage — DefaultAzureCredential with no secret anywhere in sight, and both clients built from that same credential and the same subscription ID, exactly the pattern Lesson 10 introduced.

Before creating anything, the script calls resource_groups.create_or_update against the target resource group. That call is idempotent — the exact property Chapter 1 spent an entire lesson on — so running this whole script a second time against a resource group that already exists doesn't fail or duplicate anything, it just confirms the group is still there and moves on.

Then storage_accounts.begin_create submits the real request — and hands back a poller immediately, not the finished storage account, because creating one takes real time on Azure's side. Calling poller.result() is what actually blocks until that work finishes and returns the real, finished storage account object, ready to print its name.

Boto3's version of the same job is shorter, but it follows the identical shape underneath: build a client with a region, wrap the actual call in try and except ClientError the way Chapter 1's error-handling lesson taught, and remember the one real gotcha unique to S3 — create_bucket needs a LocationConstraint argument for every AWS region except us-east-1, or the call raises a real error instead of creating the bucket.

Every piece from this chapter just did real work in one script: the right SDK, the right client, credentials with nothing hardcoded, and a resource that actually exists afterward. Chapter 4 moves to the command line directly — Lesson 13 writes a real Bash script using the az CLI itself.
